item.text: {"text":"FPMC adds a user–candidate preference score to a factorized last-item→candidate transition; its long-term component is a learned user vector, not pooled history. FOSSIL replaces that component with a normalized sum of historical item embeddings, adding recent-item transitions weighted by learned global and user-specific coefficients for each lag. Thus, combining pooled history with weighted recent items is established; a five-item exponential residual is structurally close to a constrained FOSSIL-style component. [FPMC/FOSSIL equations](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.09152). Recent approaches use richer fusion: LS4SRec (2025) uses recent-k average pooling and whole-history attention pooling as short/long-term supervision; DiffLSRec (2026) treats long-term interests as a prior and short-term interests as guidance during diffusion. [LS4SRec](https://doi.org/10.1145/3723173), [DiffLSRec](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v318/wang26a.html).\n\nSuggested minimal ablations: identical SASRec backbone plus (a) no residual, (b) last-item-only residual, (c) uniform mean of five recent embeddings, (d) normalized exp(-age) pooling of the same five. Match embedding transforms, residual scaling/tuning budget, training settings and validation candidates. Assuming age means interaction lag 0–4, normalized exponential weights assign about 63.6% to the last item, making (b) essential. To isolate ordering beyond the last item, keep the last item fixed and randomly permute the preceding four items within the residual branch only; preserve SASRec’s original input. Compare original versus shuffled assignment across repeated permutations, ideally with matched retrained controls. Exponential pooling captures lag-dependent additive effects, not interactions between recent items. Improvement over last-only supports additional-history utility; improvement over uniform and shuffled controls supports useful recency assignment. Report all four categories and macro validation HR@10; novelty requires more than adding weighted recent-item similarity."}
